Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 12, verse 111 (part 2 of 4):

﴿He said: "O good news! This is a boy."﴾ Ja'far said: God, exalted is He, had a secret concerning Joseph, peace be upon him, and He veiled from them the place of His secret. Had He unveiled for the caravan the reality of what He had deposited in that rising full moon from the tower of their bucket, their speaker would not have been content with that, nor would they have made him merchandise. For this reason, when some of the matter was unveiled to the women, they said: ﴿This is not a human; this is none but a noble angel.﴾ And because of their ignorance of what He had deposited in him of the treasuries of the unseen, they sold him for a paltry price, and this is the meaning of His words, glorified is He: ﴿and they sold him for a paltry price.﴾

Al-Junayd (may his secret be sanctified) said: Everything that falls under counting and enumeration is paltry, even if it were all that is in the two worlds. So let not your share from your Lord be paltry, such that you incline toward it and are content with it instead of your Lord, great is His majesty.

Ibn 'Ata' said: The sale by Joseph's brothers of a soul which is not fit to be sold is no more astonishing than your selling of your soul for a lowly desire, after you had sold it to your Lord for the fullest price. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their selves…﴾ (the verse). So the sale of what had already been sold is void. Rather, Joseph was sold by his enemies, while you are selling your soul to your enemies.

﴿And the one who bought him from Egypt said to his wife, "Make his lodging honorable."﴾ It was said: That is, do not look at him with a look of desire, for his face is a mirror that displays the Truth in the world. Or: do not look at him with the look of servitude, but look at him with the look of gnosis, so that you see in him the lights of lordship. Or: place his love in your heart, not in your self, for the heart is the locus of knowledge and obedience, while the self is the locus of temptation and desire.

﴿Perhaps he will benefit us.﴾ It was said: That is, by acquainting us with the stations of the truthful and the ranks of the spiritual beings, and by bringing us, through the blessing of his companionship, to the witnessing of the Lord of the worlds. It was also said: He meant the good companionship of him in this world, that perhaps he would intercede for us in the Hereafter.

﴿And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him﴾, since passion had overcome her. ﴿And she closed the doors﴾, she cut off the means and gathered her resolve toward him. Or she closed the doors of the house out of jealousy, lest anyone see their secrets. ﴿And she certainly desired him﴾. Ibn 'Ata' said: a desire of lust. ﴿And he desired her﴾, a desire of restraint from what she desired, by striking or the like. ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾, and that is the divine admonisher in his heart. ﴿Thus, that We might turn away from him evil﴾ and wicked thoughts ﴿and indecency﴾, ugly deeds. It was also said: The proof was that at that time he saw none but God, exalted and glorified is He. It was also said: it was the vision of his father Ya'qub, peace be upon him, biting his index finger. Some of our eminent shaykhs took this as one of the proofs that the well-known "rabitah" among our masters the Naqshbandis has an authentic origin; but even if this were sound, it is far removed from that.

﴿And they raced to the door﴾, fleeing from the place of danger. It was said: Had he fled to God, exalted is He, it would have sufficed him, and he would not have suffered afterward what he suffered. ﴿And they found her master at the door. She said, "What is the recompense of one who intended evil to your family, except that he be imprisoned or subjected to painful punishment?"﴾ She cleared herself of the sin, for she knew at that moment that if she showed the truth, she would be killed and deprived of the sweetness of love for Joseph and of gazing upon his face.

For your love I have loved to remain alive, my soul,
so let not my remaining last if you turn away from me.

She only hinted at attributing the sin to him, knowing that he, peace be upon him, had not been left in distress, and no one could harm him, since his face captivates hearts and draws souls.

In his glance are moments of magic,
by which he kills and gives life to whom he wills.
He captivates the worlds with his eyes,
as if the worlds were his slaves.

Ibn 'Ata' said: At that time she had not yet been fully immersed in his love, so she did not speak the truth and preferred herself over him. For this reason, when she was fully immersed in love, she preferred his self over her own, and said: ﴿Now the truth has become manifest﴾, the verse. Then, peace be upon him, after her accusation, could not do otherwise than defend the sanctity of prophethood, which is the great trust of God, exalted is He, and so he said: ﴿It was she who sought to seduce me from myself﴾. Otherwise, what befits the dignity of nobility is silence about her reply, lest he expose her. It was also said: She had claimed love for Joseph, and disowned it when the trial descended. Joseph, peace be upon him, wished to make her bear the blame of love, for blame is the emblem of lovers, and whoever is not blamed for passion is not truly realized in it. ﴿Indeed, your guile is great.﴾ The greatness of their guile is like the greatness of their guile, for when they are afflicted with love, they display of enticements what the heart finds hard to resist, what Iblis himself cannot achieve, with the assistance of nature's inclination toward them and the strong affinity between men and them, as His words, exalted is He, indicate: ﴿He created you from a single soul and created from it its mate﴾. Thus there is in the world no trial more harmful to men than women.

﴿She had indeed become passionately in love with him.﴾ Al-Junayd (may his secret be sanctified) said: Shaghaf is that the lover does not see the beloved's harshness as harshness, but sees it as justice and fidelity.

And your torment to me is sweet, and your injustice upon me,
by what desire decrees for you, is justice.

﴿Indeed, we see her in manifest error.﴾ Ibn 'Ata' said: In disturbing love. ﴿So when they saw him, they magnified him﴾, they exalted him, for they saw in his face the light of awe. ﴿And they cut their hands﴾, from being wholly absorbed in his greatness and majesty. Perhaps he unveiled to them what he had not unveiled to Zulaykha. Ibn 'Ata' said: They were astonished by Joseph and bewildered, until they cut their hands and did not feel the pain. This is the dominance of the witnessing of a created being by a created being, so how much more of one who is favored with witnessing from the Truth; it is fitting that he not be denounced if he changes and what proceeds from him proceeds. And greater than Joseph, peace be upon him, in this matter, in the sight of those with sound insight, is the Muhammadan light, radiating from the divine Light and shining within the niche of the Seal of the Messengers, peace and blessings be upon him, for by my life, he is the father of lights, and the light of Joseph in relation to his light, peace and blessings be upon him, is but a star compared to the sun of the day.

For the women of Zulaykha, had they seen his forehead,
they would have preferred hearts over hands in cutting.

And they said: ﴿This is not a human; this is none but a noble angel.﴾ They said that in exalting him, peace be upon him, from being of the human kind. Muhammad ibn 'Ali, may God be pleased with both of them, said: They meant: this is not one fit to be invited to intercourse, but rather one like him is to be honored and held free from places of suspicion. The first is more fitting with her words: ﴿That is the one about whom you blamed me﴾. She meant: had he been granted what he wanted, he would not have fallen into the trap; and how can one be blamed whose beloved is this? It was as if she indicated that she was compelled in that infatuation and excused in her excessive love for him:

O my companions, I once spoke of justice,
but since love raised me, my creed is compulsion.

In this there is also an indication that blame comes only from one who is free of love, and therefore they did not reproach her until they saw what passion had done to them. How well has it been said:

I used to laugh when people spoke of passion,
while they wept in their sorrows.
So when it was said, "This one is lovesick,"
I met them with lamentation and tears.

And the Sultan of the lovers said:

Leave off your reproach and taste the flavor of passion,
for when you have loved, then reproach me after that.

﴿He said: "My Lord, the prison is dearer to me than that to which they invite me."﴾ It was said: Because the prison is a station of intimacy, seclusion, intimate conversation, witnessing and union, whereas what they invited him to entails distance from the presence and a veil from witnessing nearness. It was also said: He sought prison so that he would be hidden from Zulaykha, and that would be a cause for the increase of her love and its transformation into a spiritual, holy love, like his father's love for him. Ibn 'Ata' said: Joseph, peace be upon him, sought this only to be freed from fornication; and perhaps had he left the choice, he would have been preserved without trial, as he had been preserved at the time of the seduction.

﴿That is from the bounty of God upon us and upon mankind.﴾ Abu 'Ali said: The best of people in state is one who sees himself under the shade of bounty and grace, not under the shade of deed and striving.

﴿O my two companions of the prison, are separate lords better, or God, the One, the Subduer?﴾ It is a call to tawhid in its most complete form. It is related that a man said to al-Fudayl: Admonish me. He recited to him this verse.

﴿And he said to the one he thought would be saved of the two: "Mention me to your lord."﴾ This was, it is said, a lapse on his part, peace be upon him, regarding what his station required, which his words also indicate. For this reason his Lord disciplined him with remaining in prison, so that he might reach the highest degrees of perfection; for prophets are held accountable even for weights of an atom, because of their rank with their Lord. His words may also be interpreted in a way that does not call for reproach, as some discerning scholars have held.

﴿Joseph, O truthful one.﴾ Abu Hafs said: The truthful one is he whose inner affair is not at variance with his outer. It was also said: He who does not contradict his words by his state. It was also said: He who spends both worlds in pleasing his beloved.

﴿And I do not absolve myself; indeed the self is ever inciting to evil, except what my Lord has mercy upon.﴾ This is an indication that the self by its nature is very inclined to desires. Abu Hafs said: The self is all darkness, and its lamp is success (tawfiq). Whoever is not accompanied by success is in darkness. The subtle deceits of the self may be concealed to the point that it commands good while concealing evil within it, and none perceives its deceits except the sharp-witted:

So oppose the self and Satan, and guard against them,
and even if both give you sincere advice, suspect them.

Some of the masters have mentioned that the self ascends, through struggle and discipline, from the station of being commanding (ammarah) to another station of being self-reproaching (lawwamah), then content and pleasing, then at peace (mutma'innah), and other states. They assigned to each station a specific remembrance and dwelt at length on this; let one refer to it there.

﴿He said: "Set me over the treasuries of the land; indeed I am a guardian, knowing."﴾ It was said: The treasuries of the land are its men; that is, appoint me over them as a trustee, for I am a guardian of what they show and knowing of what they conceal. It was also said: He meant the outward, but he indicated that he was empowered to act while not being heedless, i.e., guarding the breaths through remembrance and the thoughts through reflection, knowing the hidden secrets and the concealed mysteries.

﴿And the brothers of Joseph came, and they entered upon him, and he recognized them, while they were unaware of him.﴾ Some said: When they wronged him, their wrong became a veil between them and recognizing him; likewise sins become a veil over the way of knowing God, exalted is He.

﴿He said: "Bring me a brother of yours from your father."﴾ It is as if he, peace be upon him, commanded this in order to complete for his father, peace be upon him, the station of sorrow, which, as the Greatest Shaykh (may his secret be sanctified) said, is among the highest stations. Some said: There was a bond of love between Joseph and Ya'qub, peace and blessings be upon them both, on both sides, so that each clung to the other as the other clung to him, as is seen in some lovers with those they love. And they recited:

The madman was never in a state
except that you were as he was.
But he revealed the secret of passion,
while I have melted in concealment.

So Joseph, peace be upon him, was jealous that his father should look at his brother with the same look he gave him, and that they would thus become two partners in that; and the lover is jealous. Therefore he asked that they bring him for this reason. The truth is that the matter was by revelation, for a wisdom other than this.

﴿And indeed he is one of knowledge, for what We taught him.﴾ This is an indication to knowledge bestowed directly from God (al-'ilm al-ladunni). It is of two kinds: outward of the unseen, which is the knowledge of the subtleties of dealings, stations, states, miracles, and spiritual insights; and inward of the unseen, which is the knowledge of the hidden depths of acts, called the wisdom of gnosis, and the knowledge of attributes, called special gnosis, and the knowledge of the Essence, called tawhid, unification and detachment, and the knowledge of the secrets of eternity, called the knowledge of annihilation and subsistence. In the first two the spirit has a field; in the third, the secret (sirr); in the fourth, the secret of the secret (sirr al-sirr). The station has detailed exposition, which is to be sought in its own place.

﴿And when they entered upon Joseph, he drew his brother to himself.﴾ It is as if he, peace be upon him, did this only to acquaint him with the situation gradually, so that he could bear the burdens of joy, since sudden surprise in such matters is often

...tends to be the cause of destruction. For this reason the veils of beauty were lifted for the wayfarers (*salikin*, those travelling the spiritual path) gradually. ﴿So when he had furnished them with their provisions, he put the drinking-cup into his brother's saddlebag.﴾ It has been said that God commanded him to do this so that he would be a partner with his brothers in the outward harm, so that they would not be ashamed before him when the matter was revealed. Since Benjamin's heart was sought to be comforted by seeing Joseph, he bore the blame. And how could he not bear it, when the affliction of the one who loves is borne for a single glimpse of the beloved? The true lover prefers blame from the one who is in love with his beloved:

*I find blame in your love sweet,*
*Out of love for your remembrance, let the blamers blame me.*

It has been said that in the verse there is a subtle allusion to the fact that whoever God has chosen from eternity for His love and contemplation, He places in his saddlebag the measure of blame of both humankind and jinn. Do you not see what was done to Adam, upon him be peace, His chosen one? How He chose him, then offered him the trust which the heavens, the earth and the mountains refused to bear, and they feared it; yet he bore it. Then He stirred his desire toward a grain of wheat, then called out to him in the tongue of eternity: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and went astray.﴾ This was out of the extremity of His love for him, until He turned him away from existence and what is in it, and from what issues from it, toward Himself. Had He not unveiled His beauty to him, he would not have borne the trial of blame. This is like what Joseph, upon him be peace, did with his brother: he took him to himself, unveiled his beauty to him, addressed him with what he addressed him, then placed the cup in his saddlebag, then called out against him with theft, in order to keep him with himself. ﴿We raise whom We will in degrees, and over every possessor of knowledge is One who knows.﴾ That is, We raise their degrees in knowledge. So the wayfarers continue to ascend in knowledge, and the sacred birds of their spirits drink from the seas of His knowledge, exalted is He, according to the capacities of their crops. The degrees end with God's knowledge, for the knowledge of creatures is limited, while His knowledge, exalted is He, is unlimited. And to God all affairs return. ﴿They said: "If he steals, a brother of his stole before."﴾ Some of the masters said: since Benjamin was innocent of the theft with which he was charged, God caused them to speak until they accused Joseph, upon him be peace, of theft, though he was innocent of it. So this was in the category of "a retaliation for a retaliation," so that those who know may know that recompense is necessary.

And some of the gnostics (*'arifin*) said: they spoke truly in attributing theft to Joseph, upon him be peace, but it was the theft of the hearts of lovers and the hearts of those who love, by what He deposited in him of the beauties of eternity. ﴿He said: "God forbid that we take anyone except him with whom we found our property."﴾ The indication in this, from the Truth, mighty and majestic, is that We do not disclose Our secrets and bring near to Our presence except one who has in his heart the readiness to receive Our knowledge; or We do not choose to unveil Our beauty except one who has in his heart longing for Our union. Some of the Khurasanis said: the indication in it is that We do not take from among Our servants with the severest taking except one who claims [something] concerning Us, or reports about Us what he has no right to report or claim. Some said: except one who extends his hand to Our property and claims it for himself. Abu 'Uthman said: the indication is that We do not take from among Our servants a friend except one whom We have entrusted with Our deposits, and who guards them and does not betray them. The subtle point of the event is that he, upon him be peace, did not agree to take anyone in place of his beloved, since there is no substitute for the beloved in the law of love:

*The heart refused, except that it love Layla, so women became hateful to me,*
*Though they have no sins.*

﴿Indeed your son has stolen.﴾ Some said: they spoke the truth in this, but he stole the secrets of Joseph, upon him be peace, when he heard from him in private what he heard, and did not reveal it to them. ﴿Perhaps God will bring them all to me. Indeed He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.﴾ It is as if he, upon him be peace, when he saw the intensification of the affliction, his hope in relief grew strong, so he said what he said:

*Intensify, O crisis, that you may be relieved;*
*Your night has announced the dawn.*

And it is as if the tongue of his state says:

*The union with the beloved has drawn near and come close,*
*And it has delighted and delighted for union.*

(Page 80)

﴿And he said: "Alas for Joseph!"﴾ Some of the gnostics said: his grief was over seeing the beauty of God through the mirror of Joseph's face, and he had enjoyed that for a time, until the vicissitudes of events came between him and it. So he, upon him be peace, grieved over it, and his soul longed for what was there:

*May God water for us days and nights*
*That passed, and their remembrance made tears flow.*
*Ah, is there for them one day in time a return?*
*And for me is there a return to the land of the beloved?*

﴿And his eyes turned white from grief.﴾ He wept until it harmed his eyes, and this was so that he would not see anyone other than his beloved:

*When I became certain that I would not see you,*
*I closed my eyes and looked at no one.*

Some of the gnostics said: the wisdom in the loss of Jacob's sight and the preservation of the sight of Adam and David, upon them be peace, though they both wept for a long time, is that Jacob's weeping was weeping of grief mixed with the pain of separation, since the beauty of the Truth had been manifested through the mirror of Joseph's face. Adam's and David's weeping was not like this, for it was weeping of remorse and repentance. How far is that station from the station of passionate love! Abu Sa'id al-Qurashi said: their sight was not lost because their weeping was from the fear of God, mighty and majestic, so they were preserved; but Jacob's weeping was for the loss of a pleasure, so he was reproached. It has also been said: it is possible that the loss of his sight, upon him be peace, came from God's jealousy over him when he wept for another, even if that other was a means between them. For this reason it is reported that God revealed to him: "O Jacob, do you grieve over other than Me? By My might, I will surely take your eyes and not return them to you until you forget him." Some of the gnostics chose that this grief and weeping were only for the loss of what was disclosed to him, upon him be peace, of the manifestation of God, exalted is He, in the mirror of Joseph's face, upon him be peace. By my life, if the witness of His manifestation, exalted is He, had been at the first of the determinations and the essence of the essences of existing things, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would have forgotten what he saw, and what befell him would not have befallen him. And by God, the fine verse of my master Ibn al-Farid is apt, where he says:

*Had they let Jacob hear some charm*
*In the face of him, he would forget the Josephite beauty.*

﴿They said: "By God, you will not cease remembering Joseph until you become wasted or become among the perishing."﴾ This is from ignorance of the states of love and of what lovers are upon, for the lover nourishes himself with the remembrance of his beloved:

*If you prevent Layla and the sweetness of her speech,*
*You will not prevent from me weeping and verses.*

And when he cannot utter his remembrance with his tongue, he is absorbed in remembering it with his heart:

*He has gone, yet in my heart is a witness to him,*
*Who sets my inner thoughts aflame with his remembrance.*
*Thought has portrayed his person to me,*
*Until it is as if I see him.*

And how is the lover frightened with destruction in the love of his beloved, when his destruction is the very essence of his life, as it has been said:

*But in death for him there is ardent passion,*
*Life for the one I love, upon whom he bestowed grace.*
*Whoever has not died in his love has not lived by it,*
*And beyond gathering honey, what the bees gathered is the bees'.*

﴿He said: "I only complain of my anguish and my grief to God, and I know from God what you do not know."﴾ That is: I do not complain to anyone other than Him, for I know His jealousy, exalted is He, over His beloveds, and you know this too. Also, whoever is devoted to Him, exalted is He, He suffices him, and whoever alights at His threshold, He gives to him. Dhu al-Nun recited:

*If the noble ones set out to You one day,*
*Seeking You, state after state,*
*Then indeed our saddles have alighted, content*
*With Your judgment, neither settling nor departing.*
*So govern us as You will, and do not leave us*
*To our own management, O Lord of exaltations.*

This is the custom of lovers: when their state becomes severe, they turn to the King, the Exalted. From this:

*To God I complain of what I have met of separation,*
*Of the abundance of trials, and of the pain of patience,*
*And of a burning between the ribs and the belly,*
*Like the coals of the ghada tree, rather hotter than coals.*

It may be said: he, upon him be peace, only raised the story of his complaint to the Knower of his secret and his whispered conversation, seeking relief from what he found in that intimate conversation, as has been said:

*When people wish for rest and ease,*
*I wish to complain to Him, and He hears.*

﴿"O my sons, go and search for Joseph and his brother."﴾ It is as if he, upon him be peace, breathed the breezes of relief after the matter had been raised to his Master, mighty and majestic, and so he said that. ﴿And do not despair of God's comfort.﴾ That is, of His mercy in returning them to me, or of His mercy, exalted is He, in granting Joseph, upon him be peace, success, by removing your embarrassment when you find him. ﴿They said: "O Chief, harm has touched us and our family."﴾ They meant the harm of famine. Had they known and been fair, they would have meant the harm of your separation, for it has harmed their father and them and their family, if only they knew:

*It is enough grief for the distracted lover that he sees*
*The dwellings of the one he loves empty and desolate.*

Know that what Joseph's brothers said to him, upon him be peace, from here to "the charitable," teaches the etiquette of supplication, of returning to the great, and of addressing the masters. Whoever does not return to the door of his master in humility, need, and abasement, and belittling what appears of himself, and does not see that what comes from his master to him is by way of chance and grace and not by way of merit, will be distanced and rejected. It is fitting for the lovers of the beauty of eternity, when they enter the presence, to say: "O Chief, harm has touched us and our family, from the harm of your separation and from distance from the courtyard of your union, what the hard, deaf rocks cannot bear:

*O my two companions, what I suffer in love, if it lasts*
*On a deaf, hard rock, the rock would split.*

And let them say: ﴿We have come with meagre merchandise﴾ of flawed deeds, adulterated actions, and little knowledge, which does not encompass an atom of the lights of Your greatness; and all this is not fitting to the perfection of Your might or the majesty of Your self-sufficiency. ﴿So give us full measure﴾ of the measure of Your nearness from the heaps of Your generosity and Your grace, and bestow upon us the favours of Your contemplation. For when a creature is treated in such a way, the treatment of the Creator in this manner is more fitting. ﴿They said: "Are you indeed Joseph?"﴾ They addressed him after recognition with the address of affection, not the address of formality, and in this there is much of good opinion about him, upon him be peace:

*When affection between a people is pure, and their loyalty endures,*
*Praise becomes unwelcome.*

It may be said: when they recognized him, reverence fell away from them and zeal was stirred, so they did not speak to him in the first manner. His saying: ﴿"I am Joseph, and this is my brother"﴾ is an answer to them, but the addition ﴿"and this is my brother"﴾ has been said to be to lessen the immediate embarrassment; and it has been said: to indicate that their brotherhood is not counted as brotherhood, for true brotherhood is that in which there is no harshness. Then, when he, upon him be peace, saw

(Page 82)

their acknowledgment and their apology, he said: ﴿"No reproach upon you today. God will forgive you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful."﴾ This is among the conditions of generosity: the generous, when able, pardons. And the excuse is accepted by the noble among people.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 12, verse 111 (part 4 of 4):

Shah al-Karmani said: Whoever looks at creation with the eye of Truth does not care about their opposition, and whoever looks at them with his own eye spends his days in contention with them. Do you not see that Yusuf, peace be upon him, when he knew the courses of the decree (qada'), how he excused his brothers? ﴿Take this shirt of mine and cast it over my father's face; he will regain his sight.﴾ When he, peace be upon him, knew that his father, peace be upon him, could not bear a complete reunion all at once, he made his reunion gradual. So he sent to him his shirt. And since the source of the grief that had afflicted him was a shirt, which they brought him stained with false blood, he designated this shirt as the source of joy, rather than any other of his garments, peace be upon him, so that joy would enter him from the same direction through which sorrow had entered. ﴿And bring me all your family.﴾ The generosity of Yusuf, peace be upon him, required that he go himself to his father. Perhaps he did not do so because he knew that this would be hard on his father, due to the large number of people who would accompany him, and it was not possible for him to go to him without that. Or because in that case the public affairs would be neglected, and there was no one other than him to attend to them. It is also possible that he was inspired to do this for another wisdom. It has been said that the nature of being the beloved (al-ma'shuqiyya) required this, and that whoever sees a beloved who is merciful toward his lover... but there is in this what is not hidden.

﴿And when the caravan departed, their father said: "Indeed, I smell the scent of Yusuf."﴾ It is said that the east wind (al-Saba) asked God, exalted is He, and said: "O Lord, grant me the privilege of bringing Ya'qub the news of his son." So He permitted it, and it carried his fragrance to his nostrils, peace be upon him, while he was prostrating. So he raised his head and said that. It is as if the state of his heart were saying:

O two hills of Na'man, by God, let the breeze of the east wind pass through to its breeze,
That I may find its coolness, or that some heat from me may be cooled, upon a liver of which nothing remains but its core.
For the east wind is a breeze that, when it blows upon the soul of one who is grieved, its sorrows are dispelled.

Thus it is with the lovers of the Presence: they continually expose themselves to the gusts (nafahat) of the breeze of union from eternity. The Prayer and Peace of God be upon him (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, your Lord has gusts in the days of your time, so expose yourselves to the gusts of the Most Merciful." It is also said: the realized believer (al-mu'min al-mutahaqqiq) finds the fragrance of faith in his heart and the spirit of the knowledge that preceded him from God, exalted is He, in his secret. Yusuf, peace be upon him, found this breeze only when the Book reached its term and the days of union drew near, and the time for the passing of the days of separation and affliction arrived. Otherwise, why did he not find it, peace be upon him, when Yusuf was in the well, with only a brief moment of daylight between him and it? That is only because matters are bound to their times. On this basis are the unveilings (kashfat) of the saints: they are sometimes unveiled to them, as it has been said, the Preserved Tablet, and at other times they do not know what is beneath their feet.

﴿Then when the bearer of good news came, he cast it over his face, and he regained his sight.﴾ In this there is an allusion that the passionate, bewildered lover who awaits the meeting with the Truth, glorified is He, when his eyes have gone blind from prolonged weeping, the bearer of His self-disclosure (tajalli) comes to him, and casts upon him the shirt of His intimacy in the presences of His holiness, and he regains his sight by smelling that. There he sees the Truth through the Truth, and the veil is lifted from the eye. It is also said: he, peace be upon him, regained his sight only when he placed the shirt over his face, because he found the delight of the fragrance of the Truth, exalted is He, emanating from it, since Yusuf, peace be upon him, was the locus of His self-disclosure, majestic is His majesty. The shirt was perfumed with the scent of the gardens of His holiness, so the light of his sight, peace be upon him, returned to its channels and he saw.

﴿He said: "I will ask my Lord to forgive you. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."﴾ He promised them that until he would learn from them the sincerity of their repentance, or until he sought his Lord's permission to ask forgiveness for them, and His glorified permission would be granted, lest it be rejected, as Nuh, peace be upon him, was refused regarding his son, when God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family.﴾ Some have said: he promised them forgiveness because he had not yet finished with his joy in order to move on to seeking forgiveness. It has also been said: Yusuf hastened to ask forgiveness for them, while Ya'qub, peace be upon them both, delayed and promised, because Ya'qub had a stronger love for them, so he rebuked them by delaying, whereas Yusuf did not see them as fit for rebuke, so he overlooked them from the very first moment, or he was content with the shame that had befallen them. Their shame before him was greater than their shame before their father. And it is said in the proverb: "Shyness is enough for the one who fell short, on the day of meeting."

﴿So when they entered upon Yusuf, he drew his parents close to him.﴾ Because they had tasted the bitterness of separation, he singled them out from among them with greater nearness on the day of meeting. From this it becomes clear where the stations of lovers are on the day of union. ﴿And they fell down before him in prostration.﴾ Here the various kinds of God's majesty became manifest to them in the mirror of his face, peace be upon him, and they witnessed what the angels, peace be upon them, witnessed of Adam, peace be upon him, when they fell prostrate to him. He was at that time none other than the Kaaba of God, in which are clear signs, the Station of Ibrahim.

﴿My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom and taught me of the interpretation of dreams, Originator of the heavens and the earth, You are my Protector in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die as one submitting (muslim).﴾ Entrusting to You my whole affair, such that I have no return to myself, nor to any cause among causes, in any state whatsoever. ﴿And join me with the righteous.﴾ With those whom You have made righteous for Your Presence, whom You have stripped of the marks of creation and removed from them the follies of nature. There is no hiding what is in his, peace be upon him, placing the praise before the supplication, of courtesy, which the situation requires.

﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they associate others with Him.﴾ Some of the Sufis said: whoever turns to other than God, exalted is He, is a associator (mushrik). And one of them said:

Even if a desire for other than You were to pass through my mind by inadvertence, I would judge myself an apostate.

﴿Say: "This is my way; I call to God with insight."﴾ A declaration from God, exalted is He, and a knowledge in which there is no opposition from the self or Satan. ﴿I and whoever follows me.﴾ Some of the knowers (al-'arifin) mentioned that insight (basira) is higher than light (nur), because it is not attained by anyone who is still inclined toward what is other than God. In the verse there is an allusion that the caller to God, exalted is He, should be one who knows the way of reaching Him, glorified is He, and who knows what is obligatory for Him, exalted is He, and what is permissible and impossible for Him, majestic is His glory. The callers to God, exalted is He, today, from those who have appointed themselves to guidance by their own claim, are more ignorant than the donkey of the sage Thoma. By my life, they are in a dark error and in deserts in which even the expert guide is bewildered, and they think they are doing good works, but how evil is what they are doing!

﴿Certainly there was in their stories a lesson for people of understanding.﴾ They are those who have states among the knowers, the lovers, the patient, the truthful, and others. In them there is also a lesson for kings in spreading justice, as Yusuf, peace be upon him, did; for the pious in abandoning what the carnal soul (al-nafs al-shahwaniyya) solicits them to; for slaves in guarding the sanctity of their masters, and none is more jealous than God, exalted is He, which is why He forbade indecencies; and for those capable of pardon in forgiving whoever has wronged them, and for others in other matters. But where are those who take heed? Forms without spirits, and abodes without dwellers. Indeed we belong to God and to Him we return. This is the end.

Some of the Sufis, may God sanctify their secrets, interpreted Yusuf as the receptive heart which is in the utmost beauty; Ya'qub as the intellect; the brothers, the sons of the father's other wives, as the five outer senses, the five inner faculties, and the appetitive power; Binyamin as the practical rational faculty; Rahil, the mother of Yusuf, as the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwama); Layya as the commanding soul (al-nafs al-ammara); the well as the pit of bodily nature; the shirt that they put on Yusuf in the well as the quality of original predisposition and the innate light; the wolf as the irascible power; the false blood as its effect; the whiteness of Ya'qub's eyes as the dimming of insight and the loss of the light of reason; his purchase from the ruler of Egypt for a paltry price as nature surrendering itself to the spirit, the "ruler" who is in Egypt, the city of holiness, through the meanings that flow upon the power of thought from the spirit; the wife of the ruler as the self-reproaching soul; the tearing of the shirt from behind as the rending of the garment of the luminous quality, which comes from good character and righteous deeds; and his finding that the master was at the door as the appearance of the light of the spirit when the heart turns to it through remembrance of rational proof and the descent of holy inspiration upon it; the witness as thought, which is the cousin of the ruler's wife, or as bodily nature, which is her maternal cousin; the two companions as the power of spiritual love and the desire of the soul; the wine as the wine of passion; the bread as pleasures; the birds as the powers of bodily faculties; the kingship as the active intellect (al-'aql al-fa'al); the cows as the levels of the soul; the drinking-cup as the power of perception; the caller as the imagination (wahm); and so on in other respects. He applied the story to what he mentioned and imposed upon it the greatest of strains. How needless he was of that! And God, exalted is He, is the Guide to the straight path. There is no lord other than Him, and none is hoped for except His goodness.
